criteria.description: coverage_judge.py exposes a single public, pure, deterministic hash function reused for both v1 and v2 prompts. Same input always yields the same output; no I/O, network, time, or global mutable state. There is exactly one public hash implementation (no second copy-pasted hash routine).
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test in tests/test_coverage_judge.py calls the hash function twice on the same input and asserts equality, and asserts a different input yields a different hash; test runs offline under `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_coverage_judge.py -q` and passes.

criteria.description: judge-prompt-v1.md is copied from /Users/mattli/second-brain/products/voice-tutor/validation/coverage-experiment/judge-prompt-v1.md into the module's test fixtures directory as a committed .md fixture. NOTE: this criterion is only an existence/non-empty check of the committed fixture; byte-for-byte fidelity assurance comes SOLELY from c3's hash match, not from c2 independently.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test asserts a committed v1 fixture file exists under the tests fixtures dir, has a .md name, and is non-empty; test passes under the verifier command.

criteria.description: v1 provenance is VERIFIED (not reproduced): hashing the bytes of the COMMITTED v1 fixture (read from the tests fixtures dir, NEVER re-read from the external eval-set source path which does not exist at verifier time) with the module's single public hash function equals exactly '632b73a34b1a22b1'. This criterion is the sole authority on the hash scheme/format and the sole assurance of byte-fidelity. If it does not match, generation STOPS and surfaces the mismatch as a run-report finding rather than tuning the hash function or the prompt to force agreement.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test reads the committed v1 fixture bytes from the tests fixtures dir, FAILS (not skip/xfail) if the fixture file is absent, computes the module hash over those bytes, and asserts it == '632b73a34b1a22b1'; test passes under the verifier command. (If it could not be made to pass honestly, a run-report finding is surfaced instead of a forced pass.)

criteria.description: The v2 judge prompt is authored as a versioned in-module constant carrying a version identifier/tag. It preserves v1's topic-adjacency strictness AND adds an explicit content-match requirement: covered means the tutor's explanation is consistent with the claim's specific assertions (same substance). The v2 text explicitly states that matching topic/shape/keywords is insufficient and that an explanation substituting different list members, a different mechanism, or contradicting specifics is NOT covered even if fluent and topically adjacent. (The full semantic correctness of 'content-match' is human-/eval-judged in the later credentialed-smoke sprint; this sprint enforces only the structural floor below.)
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test asserts the v2 prompt constant (a) exists and is non-empty, (b) contains a version identifier/tag, (c) is textually DISTINCT from the copied v1 fixture text (not v1 relabeled), and (d) contains explicit language that matching topic/shape/keywords alone is insufficient AND that substituted specifics (different list members / different mechanism / contradicting details) are NOT covered. Test passes under the verifier command.

criteria.description: Both the v1 and v2 prompt hashes are produced by calling the SAME single public hash function from c1 (reuse, not two copy-pasted implementations). The v2 hash is computed over the v2 constant with a fixed, deterministic encoding, producing a stable v2 hash with no attempt to hit any particular v2 target value.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test calls the one public hash function on both the v1 fixture bytes and the v2 constant (fixed encoding); asserts the v2 hash is stable/identical across two separate calls and that v2 hash != '632b73a34b1a22b1'; test passes under the verifier command.

criteria.verifyBy: `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_coverage_judge.py -q` exits 0 with ALL pre-existing Stage-0 tests (the prior 39) still present and passing plus the new Sprint-0 tests; the existing module-scope import-hygiene/no-network guard tests remain green (confirming no network/model calls and no new forbidden module-scope imports); and there is exactly one public hash function per c1 (no duplicate hash implementation).

criteria.description: coverage_judge.py exposes a judge invocation function (e.g. judge_coverage) that takes a claim list, an indexed transcript (list of {index, role, content}), and config (model, judge-prompt version/hash), and returns a single verdict object. The Anthropic model client is constructed LAZILY inside the invocation function (function-local), never at import/module scope.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test calls the function with a mocked model client returning a well-formed response and asserts a verdict object of the documented shape is returned; plus a test asserts that importing coverage_judge constructs no Anthropic client and does not import anthropic at module scope (the seeded Stage-0 no-network/no-client-at-import tests remain green).

criteria.description: Exactly one model call is issued per judge invocation on the happy path (Haiku, temperature 0). The request passes the claims, the indexed transcript, and the module's v2 prompt specifically (not v1, not an empty/other prompt).
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test asserts the mocked model client is called exactly once for a well-formed response; asserts call kwargs include the Haiku model id and temperature 0; and asserts the request payload contains a distinctive substring of the module's v2 prompt text (e.g. its content-match language) so v1/empty prompts would fail.

criteria.description: The verdict output contains, for every input claim id exactly once, an entry {claim_id, covered: bool, turns: [int, ...]}; no claim id is missing, duplicated, or invented. The returned covered/turns values reflect the model's actual response (not hard-coded).
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test with N claims and a mocked response carrying specific per-claim values (e.g. c1 covered:true turns:[0,2]; c2 covered:false turns:[]) asserts: output has exactly N entries whose claim_id set equals the input set; each covered is a bool and turns a list of ints; AND each entry's covered/turns equals the corresponding mocked-response value exactly.

criteria.description: The verdict carries metadata: judged_at (timestamp), model (the configured model id), and judge_prompt_hash equal to the v2 prompt hash computed by the module's deterministic hash function.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test asserts returned metadata has judged_at present, model equal to the configured model, and judge_prompt_hash equal to the module's v2 hash constant/computed value (and that this differs from the v1 hash 632b73a34b1a22b1).

criteria.description: Markdown-fenced model output (```json ... ```) is stripped before parsing so a fenced but otherwise well-formed response yields the correct verdict set, reusing the seeded strip_code_fences / parse path.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test feeds a mocked response wrapped in a ```json code fence and asserts it parses to the correct verdict set without error.

criteria.description: Truncation detection: when the parsed verdict count is less than the claim count, the module detects the mismatch and triggers a bounded retry; if a subsequent response is complete, the correct full verdict set is returned. Detection is done by catching the existing typed parse error (VerdictParseError/VerdictCountError) raised by the seeded parse_verdicts(_text) — not by a parallel ad-hoc length check that bypasses the seeded defenses.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test with a mocked client whose first response has fewer verdicts than claims and whose second is complete asserts: model called twice, final returned verdict set is correct and full-count. Verified that the retry path routes through the existing parse_verdicts(_text) (e.g. the short-list case surfaces the seeded VerdictCountError internally before retrying).

criteria.description: Malformed model output (invalid JSON) triggers a bounded retry; if all attempts remain malformed, a typed error from the existing hierarchy (VerdictParseError and subclasses) is raised rather than returning a partial/garbage verdict. Parsing is delegated to the seeded parse_verdicts(_text), not reimplemented.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test with a mocked client returning malformed JSON on every attempt asserts a typed error from the existing hierarchy is raised and the model was called exactly the bounded number of times (initial + retries). Verified the error type is one raised by the seeded parse core.

criteria.description: Missing, duplicate, and unknown claim-ids in the model's verdict are surfaced via the existing typed error hierarchy and never silently accepted. Whether surfaced immediately or after retry-exhaustion is an implementation choice; the graded requirement is only that the correct typed error is raised.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic tests: (a) response missing a claim id, (b) duplicate claim id, (c) unknown claim id — each asserts the appropriate typed error from the existing hierarchy is raised (not silently swallowed), regardless of whether a retry was attempted first.

criteria.description: The retry is bounded: total model calls per invocation never exceed a fixed small documented bound (initial + a bounded number of retries, total bound >= 2), even under repeated malformed output.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic test with an always-malformed mocked client asserts the model call count equals the documented bound (>= 2 and finite) and does not loop unbounded.
